title: RemoteEvent:FireServer()
summary: Client → server message. Sends any serializable arguments to the server; Roblox automatically prepends the firing Player when the server's OnServerEvent receives it.

parameters.name: ...args
parameters.description: Any number of serializable arguments: numbers, strings, booleans, tables, Instances, Vector3s… No functions/threads. Total payload limited (~64KB).

reference.returns: None. Fire-and-forget: no confirmation, no return value. For responses, use RemoteFunction.

details.heading: The invisible player argument
details.body: The server receives `function(player, arg1, arg2, ...)` — the Player is injected by Roblox as the FIRST parameter. The client never (and cannot meaningfully) sends itself.

details.heading: Client-only
details.body: Calling FireServer from the server errors. Server→client is FireClient/FireAllClients.

explanation.whatItIs: 'Hey server, this player did/ wants X' — the client half of RemoteEvent communication.
explanation.whyItExists: Clients can't touch authoritative systems directly; they send intent, the server decides.
whenToUse: Button presses, input events, purchase requests
Anything where the server must react to a player action
whenNotToUse: When you need a reply — RemoteFunction or a follow-up FireClient
Server-to-server or script-to-script on the same side — BindableEvent / direct calls
tips: Arguments arrive shifted by one on the server: (player, ...args)
Validate EVERY argument server-side — clients can send anything
Use WaitForChild to get the remote on the client before firing
commonMistakes: Sending the player manually: FireServer(player, ...) — redundant and ignored as extra data
Firing before the server connected OnServerEvent — message lost
Sending tables expecting shared references — they're serialized/copied

examples.title: Request with arguments
examples.code:
-- Client (LocalScript):
local remote = game.ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Remotes"):WaitForChild("Buy")
remote:FireServer("Sword", 2)   -- item, quantity

-- Server (Script):
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemName, quantity)
    --   ↑ injected!     ↑ client's 1st arg   ↑ client's 2nd arg
    if typeof(itemName) ~= "string" or typeof(quantity) ~= "number" then return end
    print(player.Name, "wants", quantity, itemName)
end)
examples.whyItWorks: Roblox supplies `player` automatically and it can't be spoofed — the server always knows who fired.
examples.commonMistake: Writing OnServerEvent handlers without the leading player parameter shifts every argument.
